Reference.Title: RELATIVE ANALGESIC + RESPIRATORY EFFECTS OF PHENAZOCINE + MORPHINE
Reference.Journal: JOURNAL OF PHARMACOLOGY AND EXPERIMENTAL THERAPEUTICS
Reference.Abstract: Phenazocine [dl-2[image]-hydroxy-2(N,[beta]-phenethyl)-5,9-dimethyl-6, 7-benzomorphan HBr] a relatively new synthetic narcotic, was studied in 58 hospitalized cancer patients with chronic pain. A double-blind crossover evaluation of its analgesic potency relative to morphine was carried out in a series of 3 related sequential studies in which doses of from 1 to 6 mg of phenazocine were compared with 8 and 16 mg of morphine sulfate, all drugs being administered intramuscularly. Analgesia was measured in terms of hourly changes in the patients'' estimates of their own pain intensity. In terms of peak action, phenazocine was 4.3 times as potent as morphine. In terms of total effects, the relative potency estimate was 3.2. Few volunteered or readily apparent side effects were observed and those after phenazocine were similar to those after morphine in equi-analgesic doses. In a parallel crossover experiment, the relative potency of the 2 drugs in terms of respiratory effects was determined in 9 healthy subjects. Intra-muscular doses of from 1 to 3 mg of phenazocine were compared with 5 to 10 mg of morphine. Respiratory depression was assayed in terms of displacement after drug of alveolar ventilation-alveolar PCO2 response curves plotted automatically by an analog computor while the subject was rebreathing in a closed circle system. Phenazocine was 6.28 times as potent a respiratory depressant as morphine and thus appears to produce as much or more respiratory depression as does a comparable analgesic dose of morphine.
